name: Crimean Tatar
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Kavitskaya, Darya. 2010. Crimean Tatar (Languages of the World/Materials 477). Munich: LINCOM.
earlier_scan.note: Kavitskaya 2010 grammar covers phonology incl. stress; not freely online. Wikipedia phonology section (loaded) lacks stress.

new_statements.quote: Къырымтатар тилинде ургъу, эсасен, сёзнинъ сонъки эджасына тюше. Меселя: ма-вы́, ме-лев-ше́, о-ю́н. Башкъа тиллерден кирген сёзлерде ургъу биринджи, экинджи ве башкъа эджаларгъа тюшмек мумкюн. Меселя: ра́-дио, ком-пью́-тер, те-ле-ви́-зор. [...] Бир эджанынъ башкъа эджаларгъа коре къуветли ве девамлы айтылмасына ургъу дейлер. || Odabash & Kaya 1924: 11 §2: Слова татарского языка в первоначальной своей форме имеют ударение на последнем слоге. Слова, заимствованные из других языков, произносятся с ударением тоже на последнем слоге: لامبا — лампа, چایتیك — чайник, ژەلەتکا — желетка.
new_statements.translation: In Crimean Tatar, stress falls as a rule on the last syllable of the word. For example: ma-vı́ 'blue', me-lev-şé 'violet', o-yún 'game'. In words that have come in from other languages, stress may fall on the first, second or other syllables. For example: rá-dio, kom-pyú-ter, te-le-ví-zor. [...] The pronunciation of one syllable more strongly and longer than the other syllables is called stress. || Odabash & Kaya 1924: 'Words of the Tatar language in their basic form have stress on the last syllable. Words borrowed from other languages are also pronounced with stress on the last syllable: lampa, çaynik (teapot), jeletka (waistcoat).'
new_statements.citation: Sattarova, Milâra & Saniye Sattarova. 2020. Qırımtatar tili ve oquv. 3 sınıf, 1 qısım. Kyiv: Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine / IMZO, p. 65 (rule box 'Буны билинъиз!'); corroborated by Одабаш & Кая 1924, Руководство для обучения крымскотатарскому языку, Simferopol, p. 11 §2, and Кая 1928 (Latin-script ed.) §2, §11.
new_statements.locator: p. 65 (PDF p. 67), rule box 'Буны билинъиз!' in the lesson 'Ургъулы ве ургъусыз эджалар' (TOC p. 64)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (115 pp., ABBYY text layer). PDF p. 67 = printed p. 65, lesson 'Ургъу. Ургъунынъ ери. Ургъулы ве ургъусыз эджалар' (starts printed p. 64, exercise 80 with all-final accented list Афта́, топра́къ, къоба́, динъле́й, мында́, насиа́т, мени́м, суа́ль, тюшюне́, тере́н, зейтю́н). Page image rendered and read: the red rule box 'Буны билинъиз!' reads exactly 'Къырымтатар тилинде ургъу, эсасен, сёзнинъ сонъки эджасына тюше. Меселя: ма-вы́, ме-лев-ше́, о-ю́н. Башкъа тиллерден кирген сёзлерде ургъу биринджи, экинджи ве башкъа эджаларгъа тюшмек мумкюн. Меселя: ра́-дио, ком-пью́-тер, те-ле-ви́-зор.' and the green definition box on the same page reads 'Бир эджанынъ башкъа эджаларгъа коре къуветли в…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the final syllable of the word in native words, and stress moves rightward onto stress-bearing suffixes (plural, case, possessive) so that it stays final; certain suffixes and enclitic particles (predicative -дыр/-ым/-сынъ, question мы/ми, negative -ма/-ме, comitative -нен, emphatic -чы, adverbial -джасына) are unstressed and leave stress on the syllable before them; recent loanwords may keep non-final stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: Loanwords may be stressed on the first, second or another syllable (ра́дио, компью́тер, телеви́зор). Odabash & Kaya 1924 §2 by contrast say early loans lampa, çaynik, jeletka are pronounced with final stress. Non-stress-taking suffixes/particles (question мы/ми, negative -ма/-ме, -нен, predicative -дыр, adverbial -джасына) leave stress on the preceding syllable, giving minimal pairs like алма́ 'apple' vs а́лма 'don't take' (Sattarova & Sattarova 2019: 97; Memetov & Aliyeva 2018: 10-11).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress in citation forms; the textbook rule is stated for the word (сёз). Suffix behaviour from the other opened sources: possessive suffixes are stressed, predicative -дыр/-ым etc. are not (Memetov & Aliyeva 2018: 70; Seit-Celil 2021 charts), the question particle мы/ми, negative -ма/-ме, emphatic -чы and comitative -нен do not take stress (Kaya 1928 §2 note, §11; Seit-Celil 2020: 110, 228); compounds carry a single stress (Memetov & Aliyeva 2018: 84).
new_statements.identity_note: The 2019/2020 school grammars and the 2018-2021 textbooks describe the standard literary language (based on the Central/Orta yolaq dialect, crim1257 proper); Odabash & Kaya 1924/1928 describe the pre-standardisation literary language taught in Simferopol, also Central-dialect based. No dialect-specific (Steppe/Nogai or Southern/Yalıboyu) stress data were found.

sources.note: p. 65, rule box 'Буны билинъиз!': in Crimean Tatar stress falls, as a rule, on the last syllable of the word (ма-вы́, ме-лев-ше́, о-ю́н); in words borrowed from other languages stress may fall on the first, second or other syllables (ра́-дио, ком-пью́-тер, те-ле-ви́-зор). Also defines stress as the stronger and longer pronunciation of one syllable relative to the others.

sources.citation: Seit-Celil, Abibulla. 2021. Ecnebiyler içün qırımtatar tili [Crimean Tatar for foreigners]. Kyiv.
sources.note: Pronunciation lessons give stress-pattern charts rather than prose: p. 13 patterns ˊ / –ˊ / ––ˊ / –––ˊ (ve, ise, balalar, balalarım: final stress in 1-4-syllable words); p. 37 patterns incl. ˊ– (evdir, qızdır) and –ˊ– (anamdır, babadır) showing predicative -dır unstressed; table p. 373 marks 'Urğu avuşuvı / stress transition' for the -dır forms. Preface says the book introduces 'söz urğusınıñ esas istisnaları' (main exceptions of word stress).

sources.citation: Seit-Celil, Abibulla. 2020. Qırımtatar tili. Ögretici kitap [Crimean Tatar: a textbook, A0-B1]. Kyiv. 288 pp.
sources.note: p. 110: instrumental/comitative -nen does not take stress (studentle´rnen, özümi´znen); p. 228: 'oqumaq (urğu soñki ecağa tüşe) → oqu! (urğu negizniñ soñki ecasından evelkisine keçe)' i.e. infinitive has final stress, imperative stress retracts to the syllable before the stem-final one; negative -ma/-me and emphatic -çı/-çi do not take stress, stress stays on the preceding syllable.
